The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Restated at replacement capex: GILD spent $1,671mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $1,105mm of plant depreciation, 0.66% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge stays nil. Restated without one-off cash: GILD's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $525mm of legal settlements; $3,400mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 900mm; 2024 instalment 1,200mm; 2025 instalment 1,300mm). None recurs, so the charge stays nil. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 39.52% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 51.47%, so the charge rebuilds at -11.95%. It was held at nil, but GILD books $2,400mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0000882095-26-000006), 8.15% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -8.15%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 GILD's cash flow statement shows receivables up $71mm, inventories up $2,304mm, payables down $189mm, a working capital build of $2,564mm, 3.01% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -8.15% where the filed figures rebuild it at -11.95%, and stays there.
